design.entrypoint: packages/compare/node/bridge.mjs is the fixed installed Node entrypoint: one bounded JSON request on stdin, one bounded JSON response on stdout, exit 0 for every handled failure (ok:false + ContractError code), nonzero only when the entrypoint itself cannot run.
design.dispatch: protocol.mjs owns the closed request vocabulary (describe/normalize/align) and dispatches into the same @inkflip/compare modules the browser uses - normalizeText, checkNormalizedView, alignPage with frozen REGION_MATCH_V1 parameters. No native-only reimplementation (ADR009).
design.python_side: native/inkflip/compare_bridge.py invokes fixed argv [resolved node, repo entrypoint] with shell=False, minimal env (locale + private TMPDIR scratch, no NODE_OPTIONS/PATH), and a selectors pump that byte-counts stdout/stderr against caps, kills the child process group on overflow or the wall deadline, and reaps with a bounded wait. stdin is closed promptly so EOF semantics are exact.
design.capability: Missing/non-executable node, missing entrypoint or spawn ENOENT/EACCES -> BridgeCapabilityError('capability'). There is deliberately no Python fallback comparison algorithm.
design.identity: comparatorIdentity() rides every response: package, bridge_version 1.0.0, protocol inkflip-compare-bridge v1, normalization scalar-whitespace-v1, alignment region-match-v1, score_semantics algorithm_diagnostics_not_probability, node version + platform. BridgeResult.manifest_entry() renders it for run/comparison manifests (I13).
design.bounds: Request capped at 16 MiB pre-spawn (Python) and 32 MiB at the entrypoint; stdout capped at 16 MiB (kill -> output_limit, never truncation); stderr capped at 1 MiB with a bounded 8 KiB tail retained on the exception; element caps on raws/pages/occurrences; 60 s wall default.

limitations: Verified on macOS arm64 (Darwin 25.5.0) with node v26.7.0 only; the bridge is POSIX-only by design (process-group kill, start_new_session) - Linux verification is a coordinator dispatch, Windows is out of scope.
The entrypoint requires a Node new enough to import .ts directly (type stripping); an older runtime exits nonzero and surfaces as a typed capability/child failure, never a comparison result.

The bridge trusts its fixed entrypoint, not its payload: it defends the invocation boundary (fixed argv/env, bounded streams, process-group kill). It is not a sandbox for hostile entrypoint code - a supervised container remains the hardened route for untrusted corpora per the threat model.
Python-side caps (16 MiB request/response, 1 MiB stderr, 60 s wall) are stricter than the entrypoint's last-resort bounds; either side over its own cap is an honest typed error.
T31 ships the bridge and parity proof only; wiring it into a report/manifest writer is a later task's scope.
